answer: Jury seats come from pools partitioned by subnetwork, and no pool may supply more than 20 percent of a quorum, so a valid grade needs five independent operators. Each auditor gets a nonce-bound receipt copy, and divergence above one point triggers a third review by a pool with no prior exposure. Cost: a cartel needs 5 subnetworks, 5 stakes and 5 histories to control one quorum, against 2 stakes under a flat jury. A river of recycled attestations from one operator earns 0 of the 70 percent work share, and the nectar of a shared pool dries up once two seats trace to the same terrace.
